# LOS Companion Extension Template

A free, MIT-licensed Chrome Extension template for building companion tools on top of **any web-based Loan Origination System (LOS)** — including closed platforms with no public API and no interconnectivity.

- Repository: https://github.com/Spuds0588/los-companion-extension-template
- Landing page: https://spuds0588.github.io/los-companion-extension-template/
- License: MIT
- Author / contact: Corey Burns — burnsdevfeedback@gmail.com

## What it is

A starting point for developers, not a finished product. The template provides the platform-agnostic plumbing that is tedious and fragile to build by hand against a closed SPA, and you build your actual tool on top of it:

- **Context extraction engine:** parses the LOS URL (named capture groups: `entityId`, `entityTab`) and `localStorage` to identify the active user, record ID, and current tab/view.
- **Shadow DOM overlay injection:** declarative floating action buttons (FABs) that render over any web app without CSS bleed from the host framework.
- **Reactive side panel:** dependency-free panel synced to the user's navigation state.
- **Presence heartbeats:** visibility-aware telemetry for time tracking and workflow analytics.
- **Background message bus:** MV3 service-worker router ready for your own `fetch()` calls to CRMs, webhooks, and databases.

## Who it is for

- Teams whose LOS vendor offers **little or no interconnectivity** — no API, no webhooks, no integration marketplace.
- Developers building **personal or internal tools** where formal approval to integrate with the LOS directly would never be granted. The extension reads only what the page already exposes (URL, localStorage) and communicates through your own backend.

## Key property: platform-agnostic by design

There are no hardcoded LOS platforms anywhere in the codebase. Adaptation to any web-based LOS requires two configuration changes: add your hostnames to the `domains` list and provide a URL pattern with named capture groups — both in `config/los-config.js` (plus matching `manifest.json` host permissions). The README documents this in three steps.

## How to use

1. Copy or fork the repository (plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS — no build step, no dependencies).
2. Configure domains and URL pattern for your LOS.
3. Load unpacked in Chrome and verify context extraction in the side panel.
4. Build your features on the declarative config, message bus, and egress stub.

Full technical documentation: https://github.com/Spuds0588/los-companion-extension-template#readme

## Related project

**LOS Companion Electron Desktop Template** — the same concept as a standalone desktop app: the LOS runs side-by-side with a companion sidebar inside Electron, with an isolated session partition and a Node.js-backed API bus that bypasses browser CORS/CSP limits.
Repository: https://github.com/Spuds0588/los-companion-electron-template · Landing page: https://spuds0588.github.io/los-companion-electron-template/
